card.title: Introduction to unit crystal lattice and unit cell

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: A **crystal lattice** is the infinite, perfectly regular three-dimensional array of points — identical surroundings at every point — on which a crystalline solid is built, while the **unit cell** is its smallest repeating box: translate that one box (with lattice parameters a, b, c and angles α, β, γ) millions of times along the three axes and the whole crystal appears, which is why the cell is called the crystal's…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: - Particles per cell: simple cubic = 8 × 1/8 = 1 - bcc = 8 × 1/8 + 1 = 2 - fcc = 8 × 1/8 + 6 × 1/2 = 4 - simple cubic: r = a/2 - bcc: r = √3a/4 - fcc: r = a/(2√2) - Bragg's law: nλ = 2d sinθ

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: "A unit cell is the smallest portion of the crystal lattice which, when repeated in three dimensions, generates the entire lattice."

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***Counting NaCl's cell*** — NaCl crystallises in an fcc arrangement of Cl⁻ with Na⁺ in octahedral holes: 4 Cl⁻ + 4 Na⁺ = 4 formula units per unit cell — the number 4 that every solid-state numerical starts from.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: The unit cell is the crystal's DNA: one box carries the complete symmetry information of an infinite structure, which is why X-ray crystallography can describe a mountain of quartz from a measurement on a grain.  ·  Crystal lattice: regular 3-D array of points, identical surroundings at every point. Unit cell: smallest repeating volume; crystal = cell translated along a, b, c. Lattice parameters: a, b, c, alpha, beta, gamma. Primitive cell = corners only; bcc adds body centre; fcc adds 6 face centres. Particles per cell: simple 1 (8 x 1/8), bcc 2 (+1), fcc 4 (+6 x 1/2).…

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Count particles: corners 1/8, faces 1/2, body 1 — simple 1, bcc 2, fcc 4. Radius drill: edge a/2, body diagonal root3a/4, face diagonal a/(2root2). Seven systems mnemonic: "Cubic Tetra Ortho Mono Hexa Rhombo Tri". Sharp melting point = crystalline; softening range = amorphous.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ## 6. Common Confusions **Lattice vs unit cell:** the lattice is the infinite pattern of points; the unit cell is one repeat box of it. Saying "the unit cell is the lattice" loses the mark — one is the map, the other one tile of the map.  ·  **Lattice points are positions, not atoms:** a lattice point marks where a particle *sits*; the particle may be an atom, a molecule or a whole ion pair. Do not write "lattice points are atoms".  ·  **Shared particles are not counted whole:** a corner atom belongs to eight neighbouring cells, so only 1/8 of it lies in any one cell — counting it as 1 gives impossible particle counts.
